walkthroughs.body_html:
The Restless Earth — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Restless Earth brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Restless Earth.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is what type of margin?
options: Constructive
Destructive
Conservative
Collision

mcqs.q: What are the four pillars of food security?
options: Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
Food security just means producing enough food.
Availability (enough food exists), access (people can obtain it), utilisation (nutritional quality and absorption) and stability (consistent over time) — defined by the FAO.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.

mcqs.q: In a tropical rainforest nutrient cycle, where is most of the nutrient stored?
options: In the biomass (living plants). Litter is rapidly decomposed by warm humid conditions, and soil is leached — so cycling between biomass and litter dominates.
Most nutrients in a rainforest are stored in the soil — that's why plants grow so well.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.
Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
